title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with significant contracts, new partnerships, and a hint of competition. As the Space Force continues to funnel billions into satellite networks and resilience efforts, startups are being nudged to align with defense needs.

themes.title: Space Force's Big Spending
themes.body: The Space Force's $4.16 billion award to SpaceX for airborne target tracking is a clear signal of its commitment to enhancing surveillance capabilities. This hefty investment underscores the growing importance of satellite networks in modern military operations.

themes.title: Commercial Gatekeeping for Startups
themes.body: The Space Force's new playbook for startups is a welcome guide for those navigating the defense sector's complexities. As competition heats up, understanding these pathways could be the difference between success and obscurity.

themes.title: China's Rocket Ambitions
themes.body: China's latest batch of reusable rockets nearing launch adds another layer to the global space race. As these developments unfold, the implications for international security and commercial space endeavors will be closely watched.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Troubles
themes.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing raise questions about the U.S. military's readiness in this critical technology area. With three consecutive slips, the pressure is on to demonstrate progress before adversaries gain an edge.
